title: Prompting Time plugin manifest
description: What Prompting Time reads from a plugin's prompting-time-plugin.json to install, check, start, configure, and show it. Paths are relative to the plugin's folder.

manifest_version.description: The number of this manifest format.

name.description: The plugin's ID, which names its page's address, pt-plugin://<name>/.

version.description: The plugin's version; its release is tagged v<version>.

start.description: The command Prompting Time starts when it opens, unless a copy already runs, and stops when it quits: a path, then its arguments.

prerequisites.description: The programs Prompting Time checks for on PATH before it starts the plugin.

purpose.description: Why the plugin needs it, for the message when it is missing.

only_when.description: The program is needed only when one of the values in the settings object setting is value, as whooper-settings get prints the settings.

entry.description: The built page's HTML file, which the release archive holds.

protocol.description: The version of the messages the page and Prompting Time exchange: 2, in which the page runs the manifest's actions itself, or 1, Whooper's review messages, which Prompting Time reads until no page speaks it.

status.description: What the status action prints in status format 2, which schemas/prompting-time-status.json describes: the groups its items go in, and the actions their rows offer, which Prompting Time runs as the action's command, --item, and the item's id.

id.description: What each item names as its group.

needs_you.description: Whether the group's items wait on the user, which lists them under Needs you.

order.description: Where the group lists among the others, lowest first.

settings.description: The JSON Schema of the settings Prompting Time's form edits.

actions.description: The commands Prompting Time runs, each a path and its fixed arguments; Prompting Time adds the rest, such as a run ID.

confirm.description: Prompting Time asks the user before it runs the action, which acts outside this Mac, such as posting to GitHub.
